A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DAWA and the same joint watermarking-and-detection framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original watermark detection, text-quality, efficiency, and surrogate-model experiments in Section 6 and Appendix J.

after.justification: V5 retains original experiments and adds empirical entropy, sequence-length, deletion, and paraphrasing results in Section 6 and Appendices I–J.

M1.justification: DAWA's generation and detection procedures remain unchanged in Algorithms 1–2. V5 removes the explicit uniform-auxiliary alternative presented in v3 Appendix N, Algorithms 3–4, retaining only a brief discussion and citation.

E1.justification: C4, ELI5, Wikipedia, and WMT19 coverage is retained. V5 adds random-deletion and paraphrasing evaluation scenarios in Appendix J.1, extending the existing token-replacement coverage.

E2.justification: HCW+23, Hu et al.'s Unbiased Watermark, is newly evaluated in Figure 1 and Tables 1 and 3. KGW-1 is renamed KGW+23; EXP-edit and Gumbel-Max remain comparators.

E3.justification: V5 adds a T=500 comparison alongside T=200 and an empirical entropy measurement. Perplexity reporting changes from average to median. The principal model pairings, DAWA eta=0.2, and 50% masking with T5-large remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V5 substantially expands supplementary validation through deletion/paraphrasing robustness tests, sequence-length sensitivity, and empirical verification of the C4–ELI5 entropy distinction. Existing false-alarm, timing, surrogate-model, and prompt analyses are retained and renumbered.

E5.justification: The perplexity summary changes from an average in v3 Table 3 to an explicitly stated median in v5, revising statistical aggregation. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests; v5's checklist explicitly acknowledges their absence.

E6.justification: V5 adds HCW+23 scores and entropy, length, and attack results. Table 9 reports DAWA deletion/paraphrasing ROC-AUCs of 0.918/0.770 versus EXP-edit's 0.978/0.853. DAWA perplexity changes from 6.495 to 10.034 under the changed aggregation, while its existing main detection scores remain unchanged. KGW's Figure 1 TPR at FPR 1e-4 changes from 0.916 to 0.838, but v5 Table 7 still reports 0.916.

T1.justification: V5 removes v3 Appendix C's standalone suboptimal-detector example and proof, and Appendix H's uniform-auxiliary Lemma 6 and derivation. Principal optimality, token-level error, and robust-watermarking results and proofs remain. The main-text bijective formulation illustrates a special case of the retained general surjective theorem.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain joint watermark–detector optimization, the detectability–distortion trade-off, distribution-adaptive DAWA, and theoretical robustness extensions. V5 foregrounds distortion-free implementation and ultra-low-FPR detection without materially changing these contributions.

C2.justification: V5 interprets text quality relative to an unwatermarked perplexity reference and acknowledges weaker attack robustness than EXP-edit. Its checklist identifies untested extreme surrogate mismatch. Section 5 also newly attributes limited surrogate-approximation impact to Proposition 4, without adding a corresponding mismatch bound.

D1.justification: V5 adds a DAWA repository link and asset/licensing information, although its checklist retains future-release wording. It removes uniform-variant implementation details and the explanation that T5 replacements may preserve original tokens; this omission does not establish a changed replacement procedure.

R1.justification: V5 adds comparisons with optimization work by Takezawa, Wouters, and Cai, alongside surveys and newer watermarking studies. The uniform-auxiliary discussion now cites the authors' work in preparation. The central positioning against separately optimized schemes or detectors remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around false-positive consequences and joint optimization. Sections 5–6 are reorganized, related work and the impact statement move to appendices, and a NeurIPS checklist is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Earlier Tables 1–2 are merged, and entropy, length, and attack tables are added. Figure 1 gains a comparator curve, while Figure 5 is redrawn to illustrate a bijective mapping; figures and tables are also repositioned.

improvement.justification: The additional comparator and diagnostic experiments strengthen empirical support, particularly by exposing DAWA's deletion/paraphrasing limitations relative to EXP-edit. These gains improve the assessment of applicability around the retained core method and theory. Their value is limited by sparse new attack protocols, removed supplementary derivations, and the unresolved KGW discrepancy between Figure 1 and Table 7.
